summary: Introduces Ansible filters for transforming data (JSON to YAML, URL parsing, hashing, math), alongside Jinja2 built-ins, Python methods and custom filter plugins. Filters run on the control node, not the target.
questions: Do Jinja2 filters run on the managed host or the control node?
Can I write my own Ansible filter?

answer_card.title: What filters are and where they run
answer_card.answer_md:
Filters transform data: convert JSON to YAML, split a URL to get the hostname, hash strings, do math, and more. You can use Ansible's filters, any standard Jinja2 filter, Python methods, or custom filter plugins.

Templating happens on the **control node**, so filters run there, not on the target host.
